title: P300 dataset from Hoffmann et al 2008
description: EEG recordings from a P300-based brain-computer interface study with 8 participants, four of them disabled and four able-bodied. Each participant completed four sessions of six runs. Participants silently counted how often a prescribed image (television, telephone, lamp, door, window or radio) flashed in a random sequence, producing target and non-target events. The data were recorded at 2048 Hz from 32 EEG channels and support evaluation of P300 classification methods such as BLDA and FLDA for environment control.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Biosemi ActiveTwo system at 2048 Hz from 32 electrodes placed in the 10-20 layout, plus 2 misc channels. Six images were flashed one at a time for 100 ms with a 400 ms stimulus onset asynchrony, in random sequences. Participants silently counted the flashes of a prescribed target image. Each participant completed 4 sessions of 6 runs each, with no online feedback.
